chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated via a chain from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, prayer in congregation excels over the prayer of an individual by twenty-three degrees, such that one congregational prayer equals twenty-five prayers.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward difference between congregational prayer and individual prayer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Thawab al-A'mal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (peace be upon him) clarification that congregational prayer yields a reward twenty-three degrees higher than individual prayer, equating one congregational act to twenty-five individual ones. This specific numerical emphasis underscores the communal solidarity (*ta'awun*) and spiritual elevation central to Shia jurisprudence, highlighting the collective worship as a means of strengthening the Ummah's bond with the Divine.
